Decision report · 7 October 2026

Subscription-Level SQL Server Insights Enablement

A controlled proposal to enable automatic SQL Server VM registration as the discovery foundation for centralized security, performance and licensing insights.

Recommendation: approve a non-production pilot, with licensing safeguards and a funded remediation process. Do not enable every production subscription in one step.

Interpretation of the prefilled username: the screenshot proves that an authorized portal session can retrieve or retain the SQL administrator login. It does not prove anonymous disclosure or credential compromise. The material risk is the combination of a reachable endpoint, SQL authentication and a known administrator identifier.

Pros and cons

Benefits

  • Discovers previously unregistered SQL Server VMs.
  • Improves centralized security, performance and licensing visibility.
  • Automatically includes future eligible SQL VMs.
  • Creates standardized SQL virtual-machine management resources.
  • Registration does not restart the SQL Server service.
  • Supports governance and Azure Hybrid Benefit reporting.

Risks and limitations

  • Subscription-wide scope can include workloads without owner approval.
  • Microsoft binaries and a detection utility run on candidate VMs.
  • Registration improves visibility but does not remediate findings.
  • Newly identified usage can consume AHB capacity or incur PAYG charges.
  • Disabling future registration does not unregister processed VMs.
  • FCIs and unusual multi-instance configurations have limited support.

How to enable in the Azure portal

Before enabling

  1. Select one approved non-production subscription for the pilot.
  2. Confirm the operator has Virtual Machine Contributor, Contributor or Owner rights on the subscription.
  3. Export the current SQL VM inventory, PAYG usage and central AHB assignment utilization.
  4. Confirm whether newly discovered SQL VMs should remain PAYG or consume available AHB capacity.
  5. Inform subscription and application owners that a monthly discovery job will inspect running VMs for SQL Server.

Enable automatic registration

  1. Sign in to the Azure portal.
  2. Search for and open SQL virtual machines.
  3. Select Automatic SQL Server VM registration.
  4. Select the approved pilot subscription.
  5. Review the terms and select I accept.
  6. Select Register.

Registration does not restart the SQL Server service. Azure runs a monthly discovery job against unregistered, running VMs in the subscription.

Validate the pilot

  1. Record newly registered resources and investigate failed registrations.
  2. Compare the resulting inventory with CMDB, EDR and application-owner records.
  3. Review Database Hub security and performance findings for the expanded population.
  4. At the EA or MCA billing scope, review Reservations + Hybrid Benefit for changes in AHB utilization or PAYG cost.
  5. Obtain application-owner confirmation that no workload impact occurred.
Rollback limitation: the portal enables automatic registration, but disabling it requires Azure CLI or PowerShell. Disabling stops future discovery and does not unregister SQL VMs already processed.

Key control statement: automatic registration is a visibility control. It does not itself close security, capacity or licensing findings.

TopicAzure-native SQL VMAzure Arc-enabled SQL Server

EnablementAutomatic SQL Server VM registration at subscription levelAzure Arc machine onboarding plus SQL Server discovery or extension
Azure representationSQL virtual machine resourceSQL Server instance hosted by an Arc machine
Main valueNative management, licensing metadata and Azure-specific operational featuresHybrid inventory, assessment and governance across non-native infrastructure
Covered by subscription auto-registrationYes, for eligible running Azure VMsNo
Do not add the inventory counts without reconciliation. The visible 2,313 Arc SQL instances and 79 Azure SQL VMs are different views. An Azure VM can also be Arc-enabled, and one host can expose multiple SQL instances. Deduplicate using machine resource ID, hostname and SQL instance name.

Controlled rollout

  1. Baseline: export current inventory, findings, AHB assignments and PAYG usage.
  2. Pilot: enable one representative non-production subscription.
  3. Validate: compare results with CMDB, EDR and known SQL owners.
  4. Remediate: address registration failures and define exceptions.
  5. Expand: roll out by subscription wave after licensing and change checks.
  6. Govern: report coverage, findings, cost and remediation monthly.
Screenshot-based assessment for internal decision support. Validate findings with resource owners and authoritative configuration exports before remediation.
